items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Me, Webster Young, Tony Williams, and Bobby Hutcherson, Grachan Moncur, and Eddie Kahn. I think that was the band that I used there.

ctx.x: Did that – how far down the East Coast? Were you going to Baltimore? Were you working in Washington? Were those . . . ?

Every once in a while, something would come up. We would be working somewhere in Washington. Like the week that Martin Luther King did his speech at the Lincoln Memorial, I was in a club. I was in the Caverns, when that was open down there.

Me, Webster Young, Tony Williams, and Bobby Hutcherson, Grachan Moncur, and Eddie Kahn. I think that was the band that I used there. But it depends. It depended. When ’59 came and I signed with Blue Note – I left Prestige and signed with Blue Note, and then that very same year, the people from the Living Theater called on me to come there and look at this play called The Connection, see if I was interested in being a part of this thing.
